subject: The secret mistake I made at 2AM
preview_text: I built a feature out of pure panic. It was a mistake. And now it's the most used part of the app.
body_paragraphs: I was up at 2AM, my own thesis deadline looming. Not for school, but for this app. I was trying to build the citation generator, and I kept hitting the same wall. The formatting was perfect, but it felt... robotic. Soulless. I knew Turnitin would flag it in a heartbeat. I almost scrapped the whole thing.

In a sleep-deprived haze, I did something stupid. I fed my own half-written sentences into the AI, asking it to 'make this sound like a stressed human wrote it.' Not to polish it. To humanize it. To add the slight imperfections, the varied sentence structures, the subtle hedging that professors expect. It worked. Too well.

That 2AM panic is now the 'Humanize AI Text' button. It doesn't just avoid detection; it makes your writing sound authentically yours. It takes the AI-generated backbone and gives it a human heartbeat. That's why 50k+ students use it right before they export their final PDF.

Open the app and tap 'Humanize' on your last draft. See the difference. It’s the closest thing to a magic 'make this sound like me' button I could build. P.S. The secret is it adds strategic 'flaws' – a slightly repetitive phrase here, a conversational transition there. It’s the digital equivalent of a coffee stain on the bibliography page.
